name: Question 1
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/971ba12add67086eea1d5550efb76688f2b5b33d12dc808146b067a5de088d96.png)

What division problem is represented by the model above?
worked_solution:
We have $\frac{1}{3}$ on the left and $\frac{1}{9}$ on the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/fe5aab5aae0d5006aa707732c12e629aa546d83b7ad3204448a5e2f5b0fbfcd8.png)

The division operation splits the shaded region on the left into $3$ equal parts. So the shaded part on the left is $3$ times larger than the shaded part on the right. 

Therefore, the division problem shown is:

$$
\frac{1}{3}÷3=\frac{1}{9}
$$

a

b
13÷3=19
c
23÷3=19
d
13÷3=89
e
13÷9=13
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We have 13 on the left and 19 on the right.

The division operation splits the shaded region on the left into 3 equal parts. So the shaded part on the left is 3 times larger than the shaded part on the right.

Therefore, the division problem shown is:

13÷3=19
